reason: The observation is accurate but not this seat's to own, and the distinct fix it proposes must not be built. Verified at 1440: .b-edit is 520x337 at (734,656), computed background rgba(255,255,255,0.06), z-index 2, and rows 37/44/51 sit inside its box with their type printing through the stepper and the visibility group. That cause is one stray declaration in b.css .b-edit — 'background: var(--back)' on line 391 is overwritten by 'background: var(--fore-06)' three lines later, contradicting the rule's own comment ('It gets an opaque ground so nothing reads through'). Four other seats raised that same cause, so the only thing this finding adds is the demand that the editor reserve a band in real layout and part the rows below it, and that increment fails on three counts. (1) It reopens a locked decision: lock.md states 'Editing is moving something nearer. The date control moves the item on the measure while you hold it, and moves nothing else', marked 'not to be reopened by any seat'. (2) It breaks the strictly-proportional promise it claims to keep. The band is 337+12px against a scale of 14px per day at desk width, so every gap that crosses the editor gains about 25 phantom days: with the shift applied, 23 to 37 days reads as a 44-day void while 37 to 44 reads as seven. The scale is only preserved within the shifted group, not across the item being edited, which is the one gap the owner is looking at. (3) Simulated on the real page, the shift pushes the group past the container: .b-measure is height:1198px, computed as toDay x px + one row, and it does not grow, so 'Venue walk-through' lands on top of the footer and the undo bar and 'Wedding day' falls below the rail entirely, off the end of the measure. That trades three overlapped rows for two overlapped rows plus a broken rail plus a false distance to the anchor date. Making the plate opaque hides those three rows while the editor is open; that is a cost, but they are hidden rather than garbled, the rail keeps the true proportion, and the panel travels with the item as the stepper moves it. At a 9.5 bar that is the right trade.
sharpenedFix: Reserve space sideways, never downwards. (a) In b.css delete the stray second declaration 'background: var(--fore-06);' inside .b-edit so the opaque var(--back) already written on the rule stands; if the 6% wash is wanted, keep it as a layer over an opaque ground: background: linear-gradient(var(--fore-06), var(--fore-06)) var(--back). Verified by simulation on the real page: the panel reads clean and the ground stays correct for both ink and paper because --back carries the ground decision. (b) If the panel must additionally stop standing over rows at desk width, take the lateral route already sharpened on editor-has-no-ground-and-no-band (narrow the owner .b-item with right:376px at the existing 901px breakpoint and hang .b-edit in the freed gutter), which costs the measure nothing on its one meaningful axis. (c) Do not implement this finding's vertical band under any variant: item offsets, .b-measure height and the rail stay exactly as computed from the dates.
